oracle.method: numpy.linalg dense solve, inverse and eigenvalues of the affine equilibrium
oracle.independence_basis: Dense LAPACK solves of (I - W) x = c + u on rings of 300 to 320 variables, the exact infinity-norm condition number from the dense inverse and the exact spectral radius of |W|; independent of the production sparse solver, which shares no code with them.
oracle.historical_exposure: Historical author exposure is unrecorded and remains unknown.

reference_review.scope: Three affine equilibria on rings of 300 to 320 variables (contractive, non-contractive directed, and clamped), each with the dense solution's first six values, sum and largest magnitude, the exact infinity-norm condition number, the spectral radius of |W| and the largest absolute row sum.
reference_review.independence_basis: The retained generator builds each system's dense matrix from the declared coefficients and clamps and solves it with numpy.linalg (LAPACK), takes the condition number from the dense inverse and the spectral radius from the dense eigenvalues. It imports no Antecedent code and shares no code with the production sparse solver. The shared objects are the declared ring coefficients, the intercept and noise rules and the clamp semantics (a clamped row replaced by an identity row).
reference_review.historical_exposure: Historical author exposure is unrecorded and remains unknown. This review read the retained generator and the executing assertion in full; the generator was written by the repository author, so independence rests on method (dense versus sparse solve), not on authorship.
reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. NumPy 2.1.3 (BSD-3-Clause) is isolated locked tooling outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source or tests are stored.
reference_review.limitations: Linear rings only. The executing assertion compares values at 1e-8 and uses the condition number and spectral radius only as one-sided bounds (the product's condition estimate must lie between exact/4 and exact, its spectral bound at or above the exact radius), and the row-sum bound only for the unclamped case. The intercept and noise rules are restated in the test, not parsed from the fixture. No convergence-rate, uncertainty or calibration claim.
